daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Political analyst Andi Arief stated that Vice President Gibran needs a DPR special committee, generating fresh controversy around the vice presidency. The Constitutional Court is facing multiple constitutional challenges on electoral and legislative matters. Meanwhile, President Prabowo continues to assert direct command over forest fire response operations, ordering specialized attention to Tanjung Puting.

  • The Constitutional Court has been asked to extend DPRD terms from 2024-2029 to 2031 to prevent a two-year vacancy in regional legislatures.
  • A constitutional researcher has challenged the requirement that political parties must have physical offices, seeking to ease barriers to forming new parties.
  • The Election Law is being challenged at the Constitutional Court with a request to allow bachelor's degrees to replace high school diplomas as a requirement for presidential and vice-presidential candidates.
  • Special staff of the Papua Executive Committee have challenged the Papua Special Autonomy Law at the Constitutional Court, claiming they have not received salaries since being appointed.
  • The Attorney General's Office has examined the Bekasi City DPRD secretary and a Home Affairs Ministry employee as part of an ongoing investigation.
  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) has rescheduled the examination of Nusron Wahid for this week.
  • Multiple political parties have expressed support for Prabowo serving two terms, raising questions about whether this backing will last until 2029.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia has condemned attacks on civilian infrastructure following Houthi missile strikes on Riyadh's international airport, with the Foreign Ministry calling for restraint from all parties. The embassy in Riyadh has been instructed to remain alert to protect Indonesian citizens in Saudi Arabia. Indonesia reiterated its principled approach to diplomacy amid escalating regional tensions.

  • Indonesia has nominated its Health Minister as a candidate for WHO Director-General in a bid to strengthen Indonesia's role in global health governance.
  • Foreign Minister Arrmanatha emphasized that Palestine remains a priority in Indonesia's diplomatic agenda and confirmed the country's unwavering support for the Palestinian cause.
  • Indonesia is encouraging ASEAN to become more effective as the regional bloc approaches its 60th anniversary.
  • The Foreign Ministry reported handling 124,000 Indonesian citizen cases and reaffirmed its commitment to prioritizing consular protection.
  • Indonesia has not yet signed a contract to purchase 12 Bayraktar drones from Turkey, with negotiations still in the exploratory stage.
  • The Air Force Chief has reshuffled 11 strategic positions within the Indonesian Air Force command structure.

Other

President Prabowo has ordered priority firefighting efforts at Tanjung Puting National Park as forest fires continue across the archipelago, with the disaster agency reporting 639 hectares still burning across six provinces. The President also announced plans to increase the number of forest police and requested TNI and Polri assistance in their training. Indonesia has deployed 60,177 personnel to combat the ongoing wildfires nationwide.

  • Antam gold prices fell by Rp 20,000 per gram on Tuesday.
  • Poor air quality in Balikpapan has forced schools to reduce learning hours to protect students from haze exposure.
  • The government is promoting community oil wells and ethanol as part of its energy security strategy.
  • The Ministry of Health revealed that 9 out of 10 depression sufferers in Indonesia have not received medical treatment.
  • A blackout struck Batam after a wild animal entered a substation, prompting an apology from PLN as the cause remains under investigation.
